Also you're making a lot of assumptions about the output of this parser, e.g. that it produces tuples. Actually specifying the parser will help with that.

body:
This is quite clever. I think it works. What would break it is if there were any "are connected to the document" checks, but I couldn't find any immediately. Also note that this will cause events to fire on the element (but nobody is listening to them, so it's unobservable) and the load event to be delayed (which seems good).

It would be slightly more satisfactory to have some sort of abstract link-fetcher which consumes a struct with the relevant information, instead of consuming elements, and then both the element and the header version could be on top of that. However that seems like a large refactoring for minimal gain so I am fine with this for now.

body:
I'm unsure whether we should trust the WEBLINK spec's header processing. In particular I wonder what happens for:

```
Link: <foo>; rel=preload, <bar>; rel=preload
```

and other weird cases. My read is that "Parsing a Header Set for Links" doesn't handle this, or maybe it assumes some sort of normalized header set where this is really two headers.

To fix this I think the right strategy is to use [get, decode, and split](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-get-decode-split) and then use the RFC's "Parsing a Link Field Value" algorithm.

/cc @annevk in case he has comments.

HTTP `Link` headers, if supported, must be assumed to come - before any links in the document, in the order that they were given in the HTTP message. These - headers are to be processed according to the rules given in the relevant specifications.

- -

Registration of relation types in HTTP `Link` - headers is distinct from HTML link types, and thus their semantics can be - different from same-named HTML types.

- -

The processing of `Link` headers, in particular - their influence on a Document's script-blocking style sheet counter, is - not defined. See issue #4224 for - discussion on integrating this into the spec.

+

To process link headers given Document doc, + response, and a "pre-media" or + "media" phase:

+ +
    +

  1. Let linkObjects be the result of parsing link headers given + response's header list, as defined + in RFC 8288 appendix B.1.

    2. + +
  2. +

    For each linkObject of + linkObjects, run these steps:

    + +
      +
    1. +

      If linkObject["relation_type"] is not + "preload", then continue.

      + +

      Additional support for link types can be added here in the future.

      +
      2. + +

    2. Let attribs be + linkObject["target_attributes"].

      3. + +

    3. Let expectedPhase be "media" if either + "srcset", + "imagesrcset", or media" exist in + attribs; otherwise false.

      4. + +

    4. If expectedPhase is not phase, then + continue.

      5. + +

    5. If params includes "media" and + params["media"] does not + match the environment, then + continue.

      6. + +

    6. Let element be the result of + creating an element given document, + link, and the HTML namespace.

      7. +

    7. Set an attribute value for + element using "href" and + linkObject["target_uri"].

      8. + +

    8. Set an attribute value for + element using "rel" and + linkObject["relation_type"].

      9. + +

    9. For each entry in attribs: If + entry[0] is "as", + "type", + "crossorigin", + "imagesizes", + "blocking", + "integrity", + "imagesrcset", or + "media", then
